violations.description: OSCE-046 Pneumothorax: Expected answers are completely generic placeholders ('The investigations show findings consistent with Pneumothorax', 'Primary diagnosis: Pneumothorax. Differential diagnoses based on presentation.'). No actual radiological interpretation provided.
violations.recommendation: Replace with specific CXR interpretation using ABCDE systematic approach: (A) Trachea midline, (B) Visceral pleural line visible, no lung markings peripheral to line, size estimation (cm at apex), tension features present/absent, (C) Mediastinal shift assessment, (D) Hemidiaphragm position, (E) Subcutaneous emphysema. Management: Size-based BTS/Australian guidelines (observe <2cm vs chest drain >2cm).

violations.description: No systematic ABCDE approach demonstrated in expected answers - this is mandatory for AMC Clinical Examination CXR interpretation.
violations.recommendation: Provide step-by-step ABCDE interpretation with specific findings at each step, not generic statements.

violations.description: Differential diagnosis is placeholder text only ('Differential diagnoses based on presentation'). Should include: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax, Secondary pneumothorax (underlying lung disease - COPD, asthma, cystic fibrosis), Traumatic pneumothorax, Iatrogenic pneumothorax (post-procedure).
violations.recommendation: List specific differential diagnoses with clinical context distinguishing features (age, smoking history, underlying lung disease, trauma history).

violations.description: Management is generic placeholder ('immediate management steps, ongoing care, and monitoring'). Should specify: Size-based BTS criteria (<2cm observe with repeat CXR 4h vs >2cm chest drain), high-flow oxygen (except COPD), analgesia, admission criteria, discharge advice for primary pneumothorax (avoid flying 1 week, no diving until reviewed).
violations.recommendation: Provide specific size-based management algorithm following Australian/BTS guidelines with numerical thresholds and procedural details.

violations.description: No mention of image quality assessment (rotation, inspiration, penetration) which is mandatory first step in CXR interpretation.
violations.recommendation: Add technical assessment: 'CXR - PA/AP projection, adequate rotation (clavicular heads equidistant), inspiration (6 anterior ribs visible), adequate penetration (vertebrae just visible behind heart)' before ABCDE findings.

violations.description: No explicit assessment for tension pneumothorax features which is life-threatening and requires immediate needle decompression before imaging confirmation.
violations.recommendation: Must explicitly state tension vs simple pneumothorax assessment: 'No tension features (no mediastinal shift away, no tracheal deviation, no hemidiaphragm flattening, clinically stable)' OR 'Tension pneumothorax present - requires immediate needle decompression 2nd intercostal space mid-clavicular line BEFORE chest drain'.

violations.description: Generic vital signs provided (130/80 mmHg, 90 bpm, RR 24/min, SpO2 92%) do not reflect typical pneumothorax presentation. SpO2 92% would suggest moderate-large pneumothorax requiring intervention, not observation.
violations.recommendation: Adjust vital signs to match clinical scenario severity OR add clinical context explaining why SpO2 92% (underlying lung disease, large pneumothorax).

violations.description: RAG citations have adequate confidence (0.77-0.77) but generic textbook references (Murtagh, AMC Handbook) without specific page content validation for pneumothorax-specific management.
violations.recommendation: Validate that cited pages actually contain pneumothorax-specific BTS/Australian guidelines, size criteria, and chest drain indications.

suggestions: Add specific CXR findings using ABCDE systematic approach with measurements (e.g., '3cm pneumothorax at apex, no tension features')
Include BTS/Australian pneumothorax size criteria (<2cm vs >2cm at hilum level on erect CXR)
Specify chest drain insertion technique (Seldinger vs blunt dissection), location (safe triangle), and complications to monitor
Add patient education for primary spontaneous pneumothorax (20-50% recurrence risk, avoid flying/diving advice)
Include image quality assessment before systematic interpretation (rotation, inspiration, penetration)
Distinguish primary (young, tall, thin male, smoker) vs secondary pneumothorax (older, underlying COPD/ILD) as management differs
Add tension pneumothorax clinical features (hypotension, tachycardia, distended neck veins, tracheal deviation) as exclusion criteria before imaging
Specify observation protocol if <2cm pneumothorax: high-flow oxygen (unless COPD), repeat CXR at 4 hours, discharge if stable with 1-2 week outpatient review
strengths: Australian terminology used correctly ('pneumothorax' not 'collapsed lung')
Appropriate imaging modality (CXR) for pneumothorax diagnosis
Correct specialty (Respiratory Medicine) for OSCE station
RAG citations present with adequate confidence scores (>0.76)
Emergency presentation scenario type appropriate for acute pneumothorax
agent_evaluations.review_notes: This OSCE script fails fundamental radiology interpretation standards due to completely generic placeholder content instead of specific systematic CXR interpretation. Expected answers provide no actual radiological findings, no ABCDE approach, no size quantification, and no evidence-based management thresholds. This would NOT prepare AMC candidates for clinical examination imaging stations where systematic approach and specific measurements are mandatory for passing. Requires complete rewrite with specific CXR findings, ABCDE systematic interpretation, BTS size criteria, and tension pneumothorax exclusion. Current content score 3.5/10 reflects placeholder nature rendering OSCE non-functional for assessment purposes.

agent_evaluations.detailed_feedback: This OSCE case is a generic template without specific medication management content. The 'expected_answers.management' section states 'According to Australian guidelines for Pneumothorax: immediate management steps, ongoing care, and monitoring' but provides NO actual medications, doses, or PBS-compliant prescribing details. For a medication management expert evaluation, this is critically deficient. A pneumothorax OSCE should specify: (1) Analgesia regimen using Australian drug names (paracetamol, NOT acetaminophen), (2) Oxygen therapy parameters, (3) Post-procedural antibiotics if ICC inserted (cephazolin 2g IV, PBS code if applicable), (4) Discharge medications. The current content is placeholder text unsuitable for clinical education or examination purposes. RECOMMENDATION: Reject this item and request regeneration with complete medication management plan following eTG Respiratory guidelines.
